subject: PHYS
title: Physics – Form 3
source: National harmonised progression by week, 2 periods/week, 50 hours a year

lessons.title: Definitions, examples and units of physical quantities; scalar and vector quantities
Prefixes and standard form; basic equipment for the study of force (newton meter, balance, springs, masses)
Safety rules for working with equipment; comparison between mass and weight
Measurement of mass and conversions between units of mass
Measurement of volume, temperature and time
Definition, calculation and unit of density
Experiments to measure the density of regular and irregular objects
Applications of the density of a material in engineering works
Definition, calculation and unit of pressure; factors that affect pressure in solids; applications
Pressure in liquids: calculation, factors and characteristics
Applications of pressure in liquids; hydraulic machines
Atmospheric pressure and weather: demonstration, measurement and applications; pressure and health
Effects of pressure on boiling point; applications of high pressure

chapters.title: Module II · Elasticity and Hooke's law

lessons.title: Definition of elasticity; elastic and non-elastic materials; Hooke's law and elastic limit
F–e graphs within the elastic limit; experimental demonstration of Hooke's law; where Hooke's law applies

chapters.title: Module III · Forms and sources of energy

lessons.title: Definition and forms of energy
Sources of energy; renewable and non-renewable sources
The law of conservation of energy and its application; transducers and energy flow diagrams
Energy transformations; calculating potential (gravitational and elastic) and kinetic energy
Definition and calculation of work (force and displacement in the same direction); examples
Definition and calculation of power; power ratings of devices (electric iron, bulbs, motors)
Definition and advantages of a machine
MA, VR and efficiency, and the relationship between them
Simple machines (lever, inclined plane, pulley, hydraulic machines): experiments and calculations
Description and propagation of light; rays and beams; luminous and non-luminous sources; transparent, translucent and opaque objects; shadows
Definition and laws of reflection; experiment to show that i = r
Image formation by plane mirrors: characteristics, uses and simple calculations; curved mirrors
Refraction in everyday life; definition of refraction
Laws of refraction; refractive index and speed of light; experiment to find the refractive index of a glass block
Effects of refraction in everyday life; real and apparent depth
Total internal reflection: conditions, everyday occurrence, ray diagrams
Uses of total internal reflection; problems using sin c = 1/n
Lens action, types of lenses and definition of terms
Ray diagrams for principal foci of converging and diverging lenses; measuring the focal length of a converging lens
Image formation by converging and diverging lenses; the lens formula and magnification
Definition and demonstration of dispersion; forming a pure spectrum from white light; dispersion in nature

chapters.title: Module IV · Understanding how to go about a project

lessons.title: Technical drawing: general notions; two-dimensional diagrams and orthogonal representation
Types of technical projects and their elements; steps in planning a project
Advantages of the project; feasibility studies; the energy components of a simple technical object
Technical diagrams; movement of parts relative to others (guides, reducing friction)
New words; carrying out a project; uses and limits of measuring instruments; why and how things move; mass and volume through measurements
Observing colours of light on a CD or DVD and explaining them
Observing a pencil in a glass of water; using the image to estimate the refractive index of water
